She played the piano beautifully, as if through her music she could share what it was to be alive. It affected me more deeply than I was willing to admit, even to myself. I should have told her.

I don't remember why we fought that night, it really doesn't matter now. But know this, I blame myself for her death. If only I would have relented. If only I had tried to understand. She left in a foul mood, and wasn't thinking clearly. For that, I shall never forgive myself.

After that night, I let the house and grounds fall into disarray. None of it mattered any longer. Nothing was important without her by my side. I cut off all contact with the world outside my windows, sending my servants away to find new lives for themselves. Eventually I started avoiding this wing of the house altogether. I was hoping to find solace in distancing myself from this room, but it was to no avail.

I am left to wonder, was I in her thoughts in the moments that lead to her carriage going off the road? Was it me that distracted her from realizing the danger from the storm that raged around her?

Specific events leading to a specific moment in time. I keep asking myself... what if? Was it ordained that she was to die that night, or could I have affected the outcome?

The passage of time has done nothing to lessen my feelings of guilt and remorse, there is but one thing left for me to do to close the circle.

After so many years of pain, returning here was the first step. The next step will be my last.
